sections.html:
Ware County covers 908 square miles, more than any other county in Georgia, and a large block of that is wetland inside the Okefenokee Swamp and its federal refuge. Waycross, the seat, is the one incorporated city. Bickley, Ruskin, Jamestown and Telmore are unincorporated communities, so outside the city limits an address answers only to county rules. With the swamp so near, a buyer may ask how a given lot drains.

The middle owner-occupied home is valued at $109,500 for 2020 to 2024, close to a third of the $332,700 national figure. The county had 36,906 residents by the 2025 estimate and holds 12,957 households.

About one in seven housing units stood vacant at the 2020 count (13.9%). A balance left unpaid for several years on a vacant or inherited house can turn into a recorded lien.

sections.h2: Which offices send and collect the bill?
sections.html:
Billing and collecting belong to the tax commissioner. The assessors set values. Rates come separately from the commission and from the school board.

  • Commissioner's counter: 305 Oak Street, Suite 115A, Waycross, GA 31501. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1825, Waycross, GA 31502. Phone (912) 490-4305, weekday hours from half past eight to five.
  • Assessors: (912) 287-4383, with written appeals directed to 305 Oak St., Suite 154.
  • Online parcel search and payment: warecountytax.com. Anyone whose lender escrows the tax should call the lender before paying, so the bill is not paid twice.
  • Recorded deeds: the Clerk of Superior Court, 800 Church Street.

Find out from the commissioner if your statement includes a City of Waycross line. City, county and school freezes are all possible, so city tax can matter for houses inside Waycross.

Statements should be in the mail by September 15, with payment due November 15. Manufactured homes follow a calendar of their own: January bills, April 1 payment, and a decal handed out once the tax is paid.

For bills dated July 1, 2016 or later, these rules apply after the due date.

  • Interest builds at the Federal Reserve prime rate plus 3%.
  • A 5% penalty lands every 120 days and stops once it reaches 20% of unpaid principal.
  • A homesteaded parcel with tax under $500 owes interest but no penalty.
  • Past 90 days, a FIFA lien can be recorded at the Clerk of Superior Court, where credit bureaus can read it.

If an account stays open, the county can levy on the property. Sales take place at 305 Oak Street in the Board of Commissioners Room on a first Tuesday, following four weeks of notices in the Waycross Journal Herald. The county does not promise title, and a purchaser waits at least a year before using the land or collecting rent.

Own the house and live in it on January 1, then apply at the Tax Assessor's office. Phone the assessor first to learn the live filing deadline. Once approved, it renews every year without a new form.

  • Freeze exemptions hold the operating-tax value for county, school and city at last year's level for as long as you stay.
  • An extra local exemption for owners 62 and older with adjusted gross income of $24,000 or less takes up to $20,000 off the 40% assessed value.
  • A floating exemption for ages 62 and up with household income of $30,000 or less swaps out other state and county exemptions, and the county cautions that it may initially raise the bill.
  • Damaged timber: the commissioner's front page points to the TREES Act form from the Georgia Forestry Commission.

sections.h2: How can I challenge a valuation?
sections.html:
Count 45 days from the date printed on your assessment notice. Three grounds count: taxability, value and uniformity. A bill that simply feels too high does not qualify.

Once the assessors take a second look, the case can move to the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, then to Superior Court by written notice. You can also file a return between January 1 and April 1 that puts down a value of your own.

Before you file, gather what supports your number: recent sales of similar houses nearby, repair quotes, and photos of any damage. Send the written appeal to the Suite 154 address and keep a copy.

Ask the commissioner for a payoff figure. Your closing agent then pays it from what the buyer sends. If a levy has been threatened, check the tax sale list on the county site, since a sale date can set your timeline.

Mobile homes get their own April 1 bill and decal, so treat that account separately from the land. Buyers willing to take the house as is, and to handle the title work, can close quickly. The commissioner also keeps an excess funds list, worth checking if money may be owed to you from an earlier sale.

The usual order: ask the commissioner for a payoff on the land and any mobile home, ask the assessors whether a homestead or freeze exemption is on the parcel, order a deed copy from the Clerk of Superior Court at 800 Church Street if needed, and pass everything to the closing agent. With a cash buyer the county gets paid first at the table, a plus for a house with repair needs or renters.

sections.h2: What to bring and how a visit goes
sections.html:
Take your parcel number or the name on the bill to the commissioner's counter on Oak Street. If you plan to file a homestead application, bring your deed and proof that you live in the house. A deed copy can be ordered from the Clerk of Superior Court if yours is lost.

Owners who live elsewhere can search the parcel and pay from the county tax website, or mail a check to the post office box. Ask for a payoff in writing whenever a sale is on the calendar, because interest keeps adding up each month and the balance on closing day will differ from the figure on your last statement.

If your account has gone several years without payment, expect the office to quote each year separately along with fees. Ask staff to list them one by one so you can see how much of the total is tax and how much is penalty and interest.

faqs.q: Which month do Ware County real estate bills fall due?
faqs.a: November. The county aims to mail statements by mid-September, and manufactured homes are billed separately for April.

faqs.q: Can I pay a Ware County bill without going to Waycross?
faqs.a: Yes. Search the parcel and pay on warecountytax.com, or mail a check to P.O. Box 1825, Waycross, GA 31502. If your lender escrows the tax, check with the lender first.

faqs.q: Where is an appeal of a Ware County value sent?
faqs.a: To the Board of Tax Assessors at 305 Oak St., Suite 154, Waycross, within 45 days of the notice date.

faqs.q: Is there a penalty if only part of a Ware County bill is late?
faqs.a: Interest runs on the unpaid principal at prime plus 3%, and the 5% penalty steps (every 120 days, up to 20%) apply to what remains unpaid. Homesteaded parcels under $500 skip the penalty.

faqs.q: How do I avoid a Ware County tax sale on my house?
faqs.a: Pay the commissioner before the first-Tuesday sale date arrives. Once a lien is satisfied it comes off the sale list, and the office will quote the payoff.
